dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: praṇavādisamuccārāt plutānte śūnyabhāvanāt | śūnyayā parayā śaktyā śūnyatām eti bhairavi ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
sanskrit_variants: GRETIL, Pradīpaka and the Devanāgarī in Wallis's blog read śūnyabhāvānāt; Wallis's IAST and the Lakshmanjoo Academy read śūnyabhāvanāt ('by contemplating the void'). The meaning is the same; the latter is the grammatical form.
dharana.rendering: O Bhairavī, by fully sounding the praṇava (such as Oṃ) and contemplating emptiness at the end of its prolonged (pluta) sound, one reaches emptiness through the supreme power that is emptiness.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Lakshmanjoo (via the Lakshmanjoo Academy) names three praṇavas, Oṃ, Hūṃ and Hrīṃ, sounded long with attention resting where the sound dissolves. Singh's note gives the same three (Vedic Auṃ, Śaiva Hūṃ, Śākta Hrīṃ) and stresses that at the end of the protracted sound one contemplates the void, not the usual ardhacandra, bindu and other subtle phases.

checked_against: Lakshmanjoo lineage: Lakshmanjoo Academy page quotes verse 39 with Lakshmanjoo's commentary but does not show a dhāraṇā number on the page.
GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y13 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 39 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is one long sound tapering to nothing, and the open silence after it.
geometry.svg_hint: a horizontal wave that tapers to a thin line and then to blank space
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Sound to silence
reaction.summary: School metaphor: one drawn-out sound thins and fades, and attention rests in the open silence that remains. Not a medical or biochemical claim.

breath.lands_in: the long out-breath that carries the sound, then the quiet after it
breath.cue: Inhale easily. Let the out-breath carry a long, soft Oṃ (or hum it silently) only as long as is comfortable, then rest in the quiet before the next easy in-breath. No forced hold and no straining to make the sound longer.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Follow the sound to its end and stay where it ends
orientation.gravity: Body supported and relaxed; jaw and throat soft
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The moment the sound ends, and the silence after it
attention.secondary: Not reaching for the next thought or the next sound

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: O Bhairavī, by fully sounding the praṇava (such as Oṃ) and contemplating emptiness at the end of its prolonged (pluta) sound, one reaches emptiness through the supreme power that is emptiness.
adiyogi.method_summary: Sound a soft, drawn-out Oṃ (or another seed-syllable you have been taught), or sound it silently. At the moment the sound ends, rest in the quiet gap. Do not chase the next thought. Do not force breath retention or strain to lengthen the sound.

honesty.disclosure: Door 016 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 16 (verse 39) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.

The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Keep the sound soft and stop before the breath feels short. If you feel light-headed, return to ordinary breathing. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: Foot to calf or toes to floor; stand near a wall; or keep both feet down in [retired posture] with arms branching up.
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: Avoid pressing the raised foot into the standing knee joint. Use wall or lower foot placement if balance is unstable. General practice caution only; not medical advice.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 016: praṇava fading into void. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 16, verse 39.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Any easy seat, or lie down. The map is one long sound tapering to silence.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Body relaxed, jaw and throat soft. Eyes closed or lowered.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Easy in-breath. Let the out-breath carry a soft, long Om, aloud or silent, only as long as is comfortable. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: When the sound ends, stay right there in the quiet. Do not reach for the next thought.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: one sound thins into open silence. Metaphor only.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 39: sound the praṇava, and at the end of its prolonged sound contemplate emptiness; through that emptiness one reaches emptiness. Rest in the quiet gap. No straining.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Breathe normally for a few rounds. Open the eyes.
